'''Santiago Schnell''' <small>[[Fellow of the Royal Society of Biology|FRSB]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]]</small> (born 6 October 1971) is a Venezuelan scientist and academic administrator who was the [[provost (education)|provost]] of [[Dartmouth College]], where he also held appointments as professor of mathematics in the School of Arts and Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Dartmouth Names Santiago Schnell as Provost {{!}} Dartmouth |url=https://home.dartmouth.edu/news/2025/05/dartmouth-names-santiago-schnell-provost |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=home.dartmouth.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=University of Notre Dame |date=June 2025 |title=Schnell, dean of Notre Dame's College of Science, appointed as provost of Dartmouth |url=https://news.nd.edu/news/santiago-schnell-dean-of-notre-dames-college-of-science-appointed-as-provost-of-dartmouth-college/}}</ref>

Prior to his appointment at Dartmouth, he served as the William K. Warren Foundation Dean of the College of Science at the [[University of Notre Dame]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://news.nd.edu/news/santiago-schnell-appointed-dean-of-notre-dames-college-of-science|title=Santiago Schnell appointed dean of Notre Dame's College of Science}}</ref> Earlier in his career, he held faculty appointments at the [[University of Michigan]], where he was chair of the department of molecular and integrative physiology and the John A. Jacquez Collegiate Professor of Physiology, and at the [[University of Oxford]] as a junior research fellow at Christ Church.

Schnell resigned as [[Provost (education)|provost]] of [[Dartmouth College]] in October 2026 following an internal investigation that found he did not disclose his use of [[artificial intelligence]] in his academic writings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/10/weaverbell-klee-sharma-santiago-schnell-resigns-as-provost-of-the-college |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Schnell was born and raised in [[Caracas]], [[Venezuela]]. His early interest in science was influenced by his neighbor, Serafín Mazparrote, a Spanish biologist and educator who introduced him to field studies and scientific observation. At age 10, Schnell received a Sinclair [[ZX81]] personal computer from his father, which helped develop his interest in mathematical and computational approaches to scientific questions.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/articles/c861e2jz5q5o |title=Santiago Schnell: El biólogo y matemático venezolano que será el nuevo rector de la Universidad de Dartmouth |work=BBC Mundo |language=es}}</ref>

He earned a [[licentiate]] degree in biology from [[Simón Bolívar University (Venezuela)|Simón Bolívar University]] in 1997 and later completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in mathematics at the [[University of Oxford]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dame |first=Santiago Schnell {{!}} Template from Marketing Communications: Web {{!}} University of Notre |title=People {{!}} Schnell Lab {{!}} University of Notre Dame |url=https://schnell-lab.nd.edu/ |access-date=2026-10-03 |website=Schnell Lab at the University of Notre Dame |language=en}}</ref> His doctoral and postdoctoral research was carried out under the supervision of [[Philip Maini]], FRS, at the Wolfson Centre for Mathematical Biology at Oxford.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.nd.edu/stories/soul-of-a-scientist/|title=Soul of a Scientist - New science dean boldly asks the big questions}}</ref>

== Career ==
From 2001 to 2004, Schnell was a Junior Research Fellow at Christ Church, [[University of Oxford]], and a Research Fellow of the [[Wellcome Trust]] at the Centre for Mathematical Biology. In 2004, he joined the faculty at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] as an assistant professor of informatics and associate director of the Biocomplexity Institute.

In 2008, Schnell moved to the [[University of Michigan]], where he was appointed associate professor of molecular and integrative physiology and a Brehm Investigator in the Brehm Center for Diabetes Research. In 2013, he received a joint appointment as associate professor in the Department of Computational Medicine and Bioinformatics, and in 2015 he was promoted to professor in both departments. He was named the John A. Jacquez Collegiate Professor of Physiology in 2016 and served as chair of the Department of Molecular & Integrative Physiology from 2017 to 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uofmhealth.org/news/archive/202102/santiago-schnell-named-chair-u-m-department-molecular|title=Santiago Schnell named chair of U-M Department of Molecular & Integrative Physiology|date=18 February 2021}}</ref> During his tenure, the department received the most funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH) among physiology departments.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/molecular-integrative-physiology|title=Molecular & Integrative Physiology – Michigan Medicine}}</ref>

Schnell is a past president of the [[Society for Mathematical Biology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smb.org/presidents-of-the-society/|title=Presidents of the Society for Mathematical Biology}}</ref>  During his tenure, the society launched several new awards to recognize contributions across career stages, including the H. D. Landahl Mathematical Biophysics Award for graduate students and postdoctoral researchers, the Leah Edelstein-Keshet Prize for women in mathematical biology, the John Jungck Prize for Excellence in Education, and the SMB Fellows Program.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Society for Mathematical Biology Awards |url=https://smb.org/Prizes}}</ref> Schnell has also served as Editor-in-Chief of the journal ''[[Mathematical Biosciences]]''<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematical Biosciences – Editorial Board |url=https://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaleditorialboard.cws_home/505777/editorialboard}}</ref> and is a member of the Commission on Standards for Reporting Enzymology Data (STRENDA).<ref>{{cite web |title=STRENDA Commission – Beilstein-Institut |url=https://www.beilstein-institut.de/en/projects/strenda/commission/}}</ref>

== Research ==
Schnell's research is focused on the development of mathematical and computational models in the biomedical sciences, with the goal of improving measurement accuracy and understanding the dynamics of complex biological systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://schnell.host.dartmouth.edu/|title=Santiago Schnell's research website}}</ref> His work spans two main areas: (1) standardization of quantitative methods in biomedical research and scientometrics, and (2) mathematical modeling of reaction kinetics and intracellular processes.

He has contributed to the theoretical analysis of enzyme kinetics, particularly in the context of the Michaelis–Menten mechanism. Schnell derived a closed-form expression—now known as the Schnell-Mendoza equation—for estimating the Michaelis constant and maximum reaction velocity using time-course data under initial rate conditions.<ref>{{cite journal|title=ICEKAT: an interactive online tool for calculating initial rates from continuous enzyme kinetic traces|author1=Michael D. Olp|author2=Kelsey S. Kalous|author3=Brian C. Smith|journal=BMC Bioinformatics|year=2020|volume=21|issue=1|page=186|doi=10.1186/s12859-020-3513-y|doi-access=free |pmid=32410570|pmc=7222511}}</ref>

Schnell has also examined how the rate laws describing intracellular biochemical reactions are affected by the physicochemical conditions of the cellular environment, including macromolecular crowding. His research has addressed ambiguities in modeling reaction dynamics in non-ideal conditions, contributing to efforts to improve reproducibility in quantitative biology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sciencewatch.com/dr/fmf/2009/09julfmf/09julfmfSchnell|title=Fast Moving Fronts – 2009 in Science}}</ref>

In addition to his work on enzyme kinetics, Schnell has developed multiscale models to study developmental processes and cancer biology. His research in this area has been featured in scientific publications such as ''[[American Scientist]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.americanscientist.org/article/multiscale-modeling-in-biology|title=Multiscale Modeling in Biology|author1=Santiago Schnell|author2=Ramon Grima|author3=Philip Maini|publisher=American Scientist|year=2007}}</ref> ''Investigación y Ciencia'' (Spanish edition of ''Scientific American''), and ''Spektrum der Wissenschaft'' (Germany).

== Academic administration ==
=== University of Notre Dame ===
In 2021, Schnell was appointed the William K. Warren Foundation Dean of the College of Science at the [[University of Notre Dame]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Santiago Schnell becomes Dean of the College of Science at the University of Notre Dame |url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/molecular-integrative-physiology/news/archive/202109/dr-santiago-schell-becomes-dean-college-science-university-notre-dame}}</ref> During his tenure, the college launched several new academic and public engagement initiatives. That fall, Notre Dame established a national undergraduate minor in rare disease patient advocacy, reported to be the first program of its kind in the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Notre Dame Patient Advocacy Initiative receives founding gift from Horizon Therapeutics |url=https://news.nd.edu/news/notre-dame-patient-advocacy-initiative-receives-founding-gift-from-horizon-therapeutics/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Notre Dame Patient Advocacy Initiative receives support from Dyne Therapeutics |url=https://news.nd.edu/news/notre-dame-patient-advocacy-initiative-receives-support-from-dyne-therapeutics/}}</ref>

He contributed to securing a $20 million gift to endow the Berthiaume Institute for Precision Health, a new research center on campus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.nd.edu/news/berthiaume-familys-20-million-gift-endows-institute-for-precision-health/|title=Berthiaume family's $20 million gift endows Institute for Precision Health}}</ref> Schnell also oversaw the planning and expansion of the university’s East Campus Research Complex with the addition of a 200,000-square-foot science and engineering building.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insideindianabusiness.com/articles/notre-dame-to-expand-science-and-engineering-research-complex|title=Notre Dame to expand science and engineering research complex}}</ref>

To promote science communication and outreach, Schnell established the Notre Dame Christmas Lectures, modeled after the [[Royal Institution Christmas Lectures]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Neuroscientist unwraps the magic of science during inaugural Christmas Lecture |url=https://science.nd.edu/news/neuroscientist-unwraps-the-magic-of-science-during-inaugural-christmas-lecture/}}</ref> He also created a professorship in the public understanding of science, which was among the first such positions at a U.S. university.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/faculty-issues/teaching/2024/09/06/how-scientists-use-public-engagement-combat-misinformation/|title=Scientists Ramp Up Public Engagement to Combat Misinformation}}</ref>

In 2022, he launched the Rev. Joseph Carrier, C.S.C., Science Medal, awarded by the College of Science for sustained achievements in scientific research. The inaugural recipient was Nobel laureate [[Donna Strickland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.nd.edu/news/college-of-science-introduces-rev-joseph-carrier-c-s-c-science-medal-nobel-laureate-donna-strickland-first-recipient/|title=College of Science introduces Rev. Joseph Carrier, C.S.C., Science Medal; Nobel laureate Donna Strickland first recipient}}</ref>

=== Dartmouth College ===
On May 20, 2025, Schnell was announced as the next provost of [[Dartmouth College]], succeeding David Kotz.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mathematical biologist Santiago Schnell to serve as next provost |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2025/05/wang-mathematical-biologist-santiago-schnell-to-serve-as-next-provost |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=Mathematical biologist Santiago Schnell to serve as next provost - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref> Dartmouth announced that Schnell would join the faculty as a professor of mathematics and an adjunct professor at the [[Geisel School of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-20 |title=Dartmouth Names Santiago Schnell as Provost {{!}} Dartmouth |url=https://home.dartmouth.edu/news/2025/05/dartmouth-names-santiago-schnell-provost |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=home.dartmouth.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schnell |first=Santiago |title=Santiago Schnell {{!}} Professor of Mathematics |url=https://schnell.host.dartmouth.edu/ |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=schnell.host.dartmouth.edu |language=en}}</ref>

On October 28, 2026, it was announced that Schnell would resign from his position as provost of [[Dartmouth College]] following an internal investigation that found he had violated Dartmouth's AI policies and did not disclose his usage of AI in academic writing<ref>{{Cite web |title=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/10/weaverbell-klee-sharma-santiago-schnell-resigns-as-provost-of-the-college |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref>.

== Dartmouth resignation and AI use controversy ==
On August 26, 2026, the news website [[Semafor (website)|Semafor]] ran an audit of guest columns in newspapers, claiming several writers, including Schnell, had used a [[large language model]] to write their publications.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Albergotti |first=Reed |date=August 26, 2026 |title=AI writing has already begun to appear on the opinion pages |url=https://www.semafor.com/article/08/26/2026/ai-writing-has-already-begun-to-appear-on-oped-pages |url-status=live |access-date=October 1, 2026 |website=}}</ref> On September 21, ''[[The Dartmouth]]'' published a full report of Schnell's writing, arguing that 96% of his academic and opinion articles were written with the undisclosed use of [[Generative AI|generative artificial intelligence]]. Using the software [[Pangram (AI detector)|Pangram]], the publication claimed that several of these pieces were "100% AI-written." In response, Schnell acknowledged his use of models for "language refinement, copyediting, improving clarity and organization," but denied that his writing is wholly written by AI.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Klee |last2=Piery |first1=Alex |first2=Isabela |date=September 21, 2026 |title=Op-eds, academic articles by Provost Santiago Schnell flagged as 'AI-written' by 'near-zero error' AI detector Pangram |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/09/schnell-ai-writing |access-date=October 1, 2026 |work=[[The Dartmouth]]}}</ref> 

On October 1, 2026, Schnell apologized for not properly disclosing the use of large language models in his writing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Schnell: What I've Learned About AI and Academic Integrity |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/09/provost-schnell-letter-to-the-editor |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Schnell: What I’ve Learned About AI and Academic Integrity - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref> Several Dartmouth students and the college's chapter of the [[American Association of University Professors]] called on the college administration to remove Schnell from his current position.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palmer |first=Kathryn |title=Dartmouth Provost's 'AI Dependency' Sparks Backlash |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/governance/executive-leadership/2026/09/29/dartmouth-provosts-ai-dependency-sparks-backlash |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shanley |first=Garrett |last2=Vance |first2=Shea |date=2026-09-24 |title=Dartmouth's Provost Quietly Used AI in His Published Work. It's Touched Off a Campus Firestorm. |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/dartmouths-provost-quietly-used-ai-in-his-published-work-its-touched-off-a-campus-firestorm |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sattler |first=Leslie |date=2026-09-30 |title=Dartmouth provost exposed for using AI in op-ed about AI cheating, students want him fired |url=https://www.thecooldown.com/green-tech/dartmouth-provost-santiago-schnell-ai-cheating/ |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=The Cool Down |language=en-US}}</ref> 

On September 25, College President [[Sian Beilock]] announced that Dartmouth had launched an investigation into his academic and public writing, saying there would be a "rigorous, objective review" of his publications.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Arsenault |first=Mark |last2=Blinder |first2=Alan |date=2026-09-29 |title=Dartmouth Provost Is the Latest College Professor Examined for A.I. Use |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/29/us/college-professors-administrators-ai-dartmouth.html |access-date=2026-10-01 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hauser |first=Brooke |date=2026-09-25 |title=Dartmouth provost accused of using AI to write op-ed about AI use |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/09/25/metro/dartmouth-provost-artificial-intelligence-ai/ |access-date=2026-10-01 |work=The Boston Globe |language=en-US |issn=0743-1791}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Beilock announces committee-led review of Provost Santiago Schnell's AI use |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/09/sharma-hubbard-beilock-ai-statement |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Beilock announces committee-led review of Provost Santiago Schnell’s AI use - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2026-09-29 |title=Dartmouth College official under investigation for AI use in academic writing |url=https://www.wcax.com/2026/09/29/dartmouth-college-official-under-investigation-ai-use-academic-writing/ |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=www.wcax.com |language=en}}</ref> Schnell's case has since sparked broader debates about what, if any, constitutes ethical AI use in writing on college campuses.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-30 |title=A campus A.I. controversy is raising questions far beyond Dartmouth |url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/campus-controversy-raising-questions-far-084115370.html |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Yahoo News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Shibu |first=Sherin |date=2026-09-30 |title=This Ivy League Professor Used AI to Write an Article About the Dangers of AI Cheating. Students Pointed Out the 'Hypocrisy.' |url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/dartmouth-professor-used-ai-to-write-an-article-about-the-dangers-of-ai-hypocrisy |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Entrepreneur |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Warner |first=John |title=AI for Me, but Not for Thee |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/opinion/columns/just-visiting/2026/09/24/dartmouths-provost-has-stopped-writing |access-date=2026-10-01 |website=Inside Higher Ed |language=en}}</ref>

Schnell resigned from Dartmouth following an internal investigation that confirmed these accusations on October 28, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College |url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2026/10/weaverbell-klee-sharma-santiago-schnell-resigns-as-provost-of-the-college |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=Santiago Schnell resigns as provost of the College - The Dartmouth |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Schnell has received recognition for both his research and teaching. In 2006, he received the Faculty Award for Teaching Excellence from the School of Informatics at Indiana University. At the [[University of Michigan Medical School]], he was inducted into the League of Educational Excellence in 2013,<ref>{{Cite web |title=League of Educational Excellence Inductees |url=https://medicine.umich.edu/medschool/about/awards/league-educational-excellence}}</ref> and received the Endowment for Basic Science Teaching Award in the same year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 EBS Teaching Award Recipients |url=https://medicine.umich.edu/dept/ebs/ebs-awards/teaching-award}}</ref>

In 2010, Schnell was awarded the James S. McDonnell Foundation 21st Century Science Award for his work on network topologies associated with conformational diseases.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2010 |title=Schnell – Identification of bistable network topologies associated with toxic aggregation thresholds found in conformational diseases |url=https://grants.jsmf.org/220020223/}}</ref>

He is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Santiago Schnell FRSC – 175 Faces of Chemistry |url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-santiago-schnell-frsc |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304103056/http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/professor-santiago-schnell-frsc |archivedate=4 March 2016}}</ref> the [[Royal Society of Biology]], and the [[Royal Society of Medicine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Santiago Schnell elected Fellow of the Royal Society of Medicine |url=https://science.nd.edu/news-and-media/news/santiago-schnell-elected-fellow-of-the-royal-society-of-medicine/}}</ref> He is also a Corresponding Member of the [[Academia de Ciencias de América Latina]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACAL Venezuelan Member – Santiago Schnell |url=https://www.acal-scientia.org/en/members/schnell-santiago/}}</ref>

Schnell was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in recognition of his contributions to mathematical biology, including the modeling of biochemical reactions and estimation of kinetic parameters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nine scientists, engineers from U-M elected to AAAS |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/nine-scientists-and-engineers-u-m-elected-aaas/}}</ref>

In 2023, he received the [[Arthur T. Winfree Prize]] from the [[Society for Mathematical Biology]] for his contributions to enzyme kinetics and mathematical biology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 SMB Awards – Mathematical Biosciences |url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/mathematical-biosciences/news/2023-the-society-for-mathematical-biology-awards-congratulations-to-the-editor-in-chief-santiago-schnell-and-the-deputy-editor-richard-bertram}}</ref> That same year, he was named the recipient of the SACNAS Distinguished Scientist Award by the [[Society for Advancement of Chicanos and Native Americans in Science]], in recognition of his work on enzyme kinetics and the mathematical modeling of the [[polymerase chain reaction]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=SACNAS Selects 2023 Distinguished Awardees |url=https://www.sacnas.org/diversity-news/sacnas-2023ndistem-distinguished-awardees}}</ref>

He has also served as a visiting professor in the Department of Chemistry at the [[University of Barcelona]].

== Personal life ==
Schnell is married and has two children. According to a university profile, personal health experiences have influenced his decision to focus his research on biomedical problems, including disease detection and measurement.<ref name=":1" />

Schnell is Catholic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Liedl |first=Jonathan |date=2026-02-10 |title=Ivy League Influencer: Why This Catholic Scholar Is Trying to Save Higher Ed |url=https://www.ncregister.com/features/santiago-schnell-profile |access-date=2026-02-18 |website=NCR |language=en}}</ref>
